history: Hohhot means 'the Blue City', founded in the Ming era by Altan Khan of the Tumed; the Silver Buddha of Dazhao Temple still sits today. Here steppe and farming civilizations met; the Zhaojun Museum tells the tale of peace through marriage. Milk and mutton flavors and horse-head fiddle tunes are the city's base notes.
importance: Capital of Inner Mongolia · The Blue City
foods: Boiled lamb in clear water — the pure original taste.
A grassland feast full of ceremony.
Salty milk tea with fried millet and milk skin.
Lamb-and-scallion shaomai with brick tea — the king of breakfast.
Hui-style baked bun stuffed with spicy paste.
Lamb offal soup with crispy baked buns.
Grassland dairy treats — sweet and bouncy.
Milk tea in a copper pot boiled with beef jerky and milk skin.
scenes: Ming-era Tibetan Buddhist temple — silver Buddha, dragon carving and murals.
Wang Zhaojun's tomb, the 'Green Mound' of peace-through-marriage lore.
Ming-Qing old street beside Dazhao Temple.
The grassland nearest a city — try a yurt.
Vajra-seat stupa with a Mongolian star chart.
